statement: The analysis is for finite static exact-potential games, described by the authors as a stepping stone toward the Markov setting.
Algorithm 1 performs symmetric parallel independent NPG updates using each agent's marginalized utility and entropy-regularized multiplicative policy update.
conditions: Uniform initialization in the stated procedure
limits: Exact utility feedback rather than sampled MARL trajectories

statement: Theorem 3.1 bounds the time-average QRE gap under the stated step-size condition, yielding sublinear convergence of average iterates.
conditions: Step size at most the stated bound
limits: Average-gap result; not last-iterate linear convergence

statement: Corollary 3.2 gives O(min{sqrt(N),Phi_max} Phi_max/(tau^2 epsilon^2)) iterations for average epsilon-QRE gap from uniform initialization.
limits: Constants/log factors and average gap matter

statement: Choosing tau proportional to epsilon/log|A| yields a tilde-O(min{sqrt(N),Phi_max} Phi_max/epsilon^4) average approximate-NE guarantee; for bounded identical-interest games Phi_max=1 makes the rate dimension-free up to logarithms.
conditions: Bounded identical-interest special case for dimension-free statement
limits: Does not give a generic linear rate

statement: The numerical study uses N=4, 20 actions, Beta(1/2,1/2) potential entries, 10 runs, and compares direct PG with NPG at several entropy values over 30,000 iterations.
A rate whose expression depends favorably on N is not empirical or formal evidence that one learned policy transfers to unseen agent counts; the paper fixes one static game dimension per run.
conditions: Separate complexity scaling from cross-N generalization
